# pheno-tokio-base

Opinionated Tokio runtime for pheno services. Provides signal handling
(SIGTERM/SIGINT), graceful shutdown via `CancellationToken`, and a
runtime builder with worker-thread count and name prefix. Zero
abstractions over Tokio — just the ergonomics pheno services need.

## Install

```toml
[dependencies]
pheno-tokio-base = { path = "../pheno-tokio-base" }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
```

## Public API

```rust
use pheno_tokio_base::{runtime, shutdown_signal, CancellationToken};

let rt = runtime();        // multi-threaded, all CPUs, "pheno-" name prefix
let token = CancellationToken::new();

rt.spawn(async move {
    tokio::select! {
        _ = shutdown_signal() => { /* SIGTERM/SIGINT */ }
        _ = token.cancelled() => { /* programmatic cancel */ }
    }
});
```

## Usage (in an Axum app)

```rust
use pheno_axum_stack::app;
use pheno_tokio_base::{runtime, shutdown_signal};

fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let rt = runtime();
    rt.block_on(async {
        let app = app();
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("0.0.0.0:8080").await?;
        axum::serve(listener, app)
            .with_graceful_shutdown(shutdown_signal())
            .await
    })
}
```

## Scope-out

- Not a Tokio alternative. Tokio is the only runtime.
- No custom scheduler. Uses `tokio::runtime::Builder::multi_thread()`.
- No metrics/tracing here. Use `pheno-tracing` for that.

## Tests

2/2 unit tests pass. Test commands: `cargo test -p pheno-tokio-base`.
